Loss-of-function variants in RYR1 disrupt calcium signaling in skeletal muscle, impairing excitation-contraction coupling and causing multicore myopathy. Both diseases converge on the dysregulation of calcium signaling pathways.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of a patient with catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia caused by a loss-of-function RYR2 mutation, or a patient with congenital multicore myopathy with external ophthalmoplegia caused by a gain-of-function RYR1 mutation, would falsify the proposed directionality for these genes. _(variant: High frequency (e.g., > 0.01%) of pathogenic variants in RYR1 or RYR2 in relevant populations.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared pathway of calcium signaling dysregulation, despite different functional consequences of mutations in RYR1 and RYR2, could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting downstream effectors or modulators of calcium handling for both cardiac and muscle disorders.
